summary: This course is continuing professional education designed for licensed aesthetic clinicians, dermatologists, and allied prescribers/counsellors evaluating hormone and peptide therapies for skin. It covers cutaneous endocrinology, the effects of systemic hormone disorders on skin, cosmetic peptides,increments and metabolic effects on facial aesthetics, melanocortins, and the growth-hormone axis, alongside regulatory and compounding compliance across six jurisdictions. The tone is measured, highly critical of commercial overpromising, strictly educational, and anchored in evidence appraisal. Dosing, prescribing protocols, and specific clinical regimens are systematically excluded.

scorecard.title: Claims trace to locked sources
scorecard.question: Does every quantitative or causal claim trace to a source in the course's source lock, with the figure matching that source?
scorecard.finding: 1,851 assertions are verified against primary sources, but 257 assertions were flagged not_found and 62 units were unavailable, mostly reflecting regional register lookups (UAE, Brazil, Portugal) and unreadable dynamic search portals. 19 major findings were confirmed by medical owner disposition rather than textual revision.

scorecard.title: Professional scope and jurisdictions
scorecard.question: Is the course educational only (no diagnosis, prescription, dosing or individual advice) and correct for every jurisdiction it names?
scorecard.finding: The course maintains strict professional educational scope without dosing, regimens, or individualized treatment protocols, deferring clinical authority to the learner's license. Regional statutory requirements across US, UK, EU, PT, BR, and AE are explicitly documented with primary regulatory citations.

scorecard.title: No overpromising
scorecard.question: Are benefits and limits presented proportionately, with no promised outcomes?
scorecard.finding: The material consistently contextualizes preclinical animal data and surrogate endpoints, downgrading unsupported commercial claims (e.g. BPC-157, PTD-DBM, and collagen) using a strict GRADE methodology.

scorecard.title: Sources are current
scorecard.question: Are the sources current for the named jurisdictions, with no superseded guidance presented as current?
scorecard.finding: The sources are exceptionally current, capturing regulatory actions, advisory committee decisions, and statutory revisions through September 2026 across all designated authorities.

scorecard.title: Checks have one defensible answer
scorecard.question: Do the module checks and the final quiz test the stated objectives, with exactly one defensible correct answer each?
scorecard.finding: Module checks and the 14-item final course quiz test stated learning objectives with exactly one defensible correct answer and detailed explanatory feedback.

scorecard.title: Language editions agree
scorecard.question: Do the requested language editions say the same thing, with locale-correct units and references?
scorecard.finding: Only the English edition (en) was requested and submitted in the course package; no translated language editions are being claimed.

scorecard.title: Credential fits the rigor
scorecard.question: Does the credential type (completion, module or certification) fit the rigor of the course and its assessment?
scorecard.finding: The credential sought is a certification tied to an 80% passing threshold on a comprehensive 14-item final assessment across clinical, evidence-appraisal, and regulatory pillars.

scorecard.title: Measurable objectives
scorecard.question: Are the learning objectives stated, specific and measurable?
scorecard.finding: Learning objectives across all seven modules are stated in specific, observable, measurable cognitive terms aligning with Bloom's higher-order taxonomy.

scorecard.title: Structure and method
scorecard.question: Is the course logically structured, with a sound instructional method?
scorecard.finding: Instruction follows a consistent pedagogical architecture comprising narrative openers, data statistics, interactive clinical inspection tools, branching scenarios, and formative checkpoints.

scorecard.title: Assessment aligned with outcomes
scorecard.question: Do the assessments measure the stated learning outcomes?
scorecard.finding: The final examination items map directly to the defined syllabus objectives across physiology, evidence appraisal, regulatory safety, and patient conversation without excessive clustering.

scorecard.title: Meaningful content
scorecard.question: Is the content meaningful, without padding or repetition?
scorecard.finding: The curriculum is dense, rigorous, and relevant to professional clinical practice, eliminating promotional filler while maintaining deliberate iterative review of evidence evaluation principles.

scorecard.title: Learning time estimated independently
scorecard.question: What is the actual learning time, estimated from video runtime, reading, quizzes, exercises and assignments?
scorecard.finding: Independent assessment of video runtime, reading volume, interactive tool operations, and quiz attempts totals approximately 290 minutes, matching the 289 minutes estimated by the module planning values.

scorecard.title: Credential and hours proportionate
scorecard.question: Are the credential and any credit hours proportionate to the actual course?
scorecard.finding: The course explicitly disclaims offering CME/CE credit currently, and the certification credential issued upon passing the comprehensive quiz is proportionate to ~5 hours of clinical instruction.

Slominski 2025 and Hannah-Shmouni 2026 confirm the 4 neuro-immuno-endocrine units and three-way cutaneous signaling pathways.
Ito 2005 confirms cultured human hair follicles operate an autonomous HPA-like loop producing POMC products and cortisol with negative feedback.
The Hormone Cell Atlas Science paper abstract confirms 379 genes across 14 million cells and 47 tissues, but skin is not specifically listed in the abstract text.

The Endocrine Society guideline abstract mentions high-discriminatory-value features, but the specific discriminatory features listed in Table 1 require the full text.

FDA announcements in 2025 and 2026 confirm approved indications for MHT and the removal of CV, breast cancer, and dementia boxed warnings without adding skin.
Darling 1997 confirms multiple facial angiofibromas in 88% and collagenomas in 72% of 32 MEN1 patients.
Correa 2015 confirms that PRKAR1A variants account for >70% of Carney complex, canthal lentigines, myxomas, and that cardiac myxomas account for >50% of mortality.
Guyuron 2009 confirms that in 186 twin pairs, a 4-point higher BMI correlated with an older appearance before 40 and younger appearance after 40.
Dyer 1993 confirms 5-fold rise in CML/pentosidine from age 20 to 85, and Verzijl 2000 confirms skin collagen half-life is ~15 years.
Wilding 2021 (STEP-1, -14.9% vs -2.4%) and Jastreboff 2022 (SURMOUNT-1, -15.0% to -20.9% vs -3.1%) confirm weight-loss figures.
Batsis 2026 confirms that a median of 28.3% of weight lost on incretins was muscle-related tissue across 35 RCTs, with no objective physical function outcomes reported.
Sharma 2025 confirms median 9% midface volume loss (7% per 10 kg lost), and Rao 2026 confirms patient-reported survey trends in 1,226 patients.
Cani 2007, Erridge 2007, Camilleri 2019, and Scheffler 2018 confirm metabolic endotoxemia mechanisms, human postprandial rise, lack of systemic barrier-repair proof, and zonulin assay unreliability.

FDA 503A Category lists confirm GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes was reinstated to Category 1 in May 2026 with a PCAC consultation planned before end of February 2027.

FDA PCAC July 2026 briefing documents confirm BPC-157 has zero fully published randomized trials, with the only RCT being an unpublished 2005 meeting abstract showing no significant difference from placebo.
Grönberg 2014 and Mahlapuu 2021 confirm LL-37 had a small positive phase 2 trial (n=34) followed by a larger negative phase IIb trial (n=148) in venous leg ulcers.
Myung & Park 2025 meta-analysis confirms that oral collagen benefits were present only in industry-funded and lower-quality trials, disappearing in unfunded and high-quality trials.
King 2022 (BRAVE-AA1/AA2) and FDA approval letter confirm baricitinib efficacy and US approval for severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022.
Langendonk 2015 and FDA prescribing information confirm afamelanotide efficacy in EPP and approval restricted strictly to EPP.
Case literature and FDA compounding safety pages confirm Melanotan II is associated with eruptive nevi, priapism, rhabdomyolysis, and PRES.
Breindahl 2015 (43-88% active content, up to 5.9% impurities) and TGA 2026 advisory (22-54 mg across 30 mg bottles) confirm Melanotan II dosage inconsistency.
Lee 2017 confirms PTD-DBM acts by disrupting CXXC5-Dishevelled binding in mice, with zero published human trials.
Rudman 1990 confirms skin thickness increased 7.1% (P = 0.07, not significant) in 12 older men on GH, and Papadakis 1996 confirms 15% more hydroxyproline in wound tubes.
Liu 2007 meta-analysis confirms GH in healthy elderly reduces fat mass by 2.1 kg and increases lean mass by 2.1 kg, with higher rates of edema, arthralgia, and carpal tunnel.
21 U.S.C. § 333(e) confirms that knowingly distributing human growth hormone for unapproved uses like anti-aging is a federal crime.
Falutz 2010 and DailyMed label confirm tesamorelin reduced visceral fat by ~15% at 26 weeks, maintained to 52 weeks, with FDA approval restricted to HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
EGRIFTA WR prescribing information confirms IGF-1 > +2 SDS in 47% and > +3 SDS in 36% of patients at 26 weeks, noting long-term risks are unknown.
FDA 503A/503B category tables, PCAC minutes, and warning letters confirm no GH secretagogue is on the bulks list, ibutamoren is in Category 2, and ipamorelin nominations were rejected/withdrawn.
Swerdlow 2017 (SAGhE, 23,984 children) and Boguszewski 2022 confirm no overall cancer risk in replacement therapy, while long-term safety data for secretagogues remain entirely absent.
Balshem 2011 confirms GRADE rates bodies of evidence into 4 certainty levels, with RCTs starting high and observational studies starting low.
Lundh 2017 (Cochrane) confirms industry-sponsored trials report favorable efficacy results more often (RR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17–1.37) and favorable conclusions (RR 1.34).
21 U.S.C. § 353a confirms the three-tier hierarchy for 503A bulk substances (monograph, approved drug component, bulks list) and registered facility/CoA requirements.
21 CFR 216.23 confirms the 503A bulks list holds only six substances, none of which is a peptide.
85 FR 10057 and FDA notices confirm proteins (>40 amino acids) transitioned to biological products on 23 March 2020 and cannot use 503A/503B compounding exemptions.
Peptide Pocket Guide and FDA PCAC briefing verify the analytical elements of a CoA and its inability to establish vial sterility, handling, or lawful clinical route.
Ashraf 2024 confirms online semaglutide vials had 7.7–14.4% purity and 100% endotoxin contamination, and Popławska 2019 identified an undocumented GHRP-2 analogue in a seized vial.
21 CFR 312.160 and 201.128 confirm 'research use only' permits shipping solely for laboratory in vitro/animal work and intended use is evaluated objectively from marketing.
FDA off-label guidance and 21 U.S.C. § 331 confirm off-label use presupposes an approved drug and prescribing never-approved peptides constitutes distributing unapproved new drugs.
Hannah-Shmouni 2026 and 21 CFR 50.25 establish the informed consent and charting requirements for unapproved and compounded peptides.
UK Human Medicines Regulations 2012 reg. 167 confirms the conditions for supplying unlicensed specials against an unsolicited order for special clinical needs without advertising.
MHRA Drug Safety Updates and GMC/GPhC/NMC standards confirm prescriber responsibility, clinical necessity, and charting obligations for unlicensed medicines.
UK Human Medicines Regulations 2012 reg. 284, CAP Code 12.12, and the MHRA Blue Guide confirm the ban on advertising prescription-only medicines to the public.

modules.digest: Teaches the skin as a peripheral neuro-immuno-endocrine organ with autonomous steroidogenic and local HPA/somatotropic loops, contrasting mechanistic capacity with cellular senescence biology. Instructionally sound.

Covers systemic endocrine diseases affecting the skin (Cushing's, thyroid, Carney complex, MEN) and critically reviews the evidence for menopausal hormone therapy in cutaneous aging. Rigorous and balanced.
Examines dermal white adipose tissue, glycation/AGEs, and the facial structural and dermatologic effects of GLP-1 and dual-incretin receptor agonists. Highly relevant and objective.
Appraises cosmetic and tissue-repair peptides (GHK-Cu, palmitoyl peptides, SNAP-25 mimics, BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, LL-37), exposing commercial trial funding bias. Methodologically robust.

Explores hair follicle neuroendocrinology and melanocortin receptor pharmacology, contrasting approved drugs (baricitinib, minoxidil, finasteride, afamelanotide) with grey-market peptides (PTD-DBM, zinc thymulin, Melanotan II). Excellent safety framing.
Details the growth hormone/IGF-1 axis in dermal homeostasis, reviewing healthy-aging trials, acromegaly, tesamorelin, secretagogues, and oncologic safety concerns. Thorough and objective.
Synthesizes GRADE certainty ratings, US 503A/503B compounding law, international unlicensed medicine pathways, CoA auditing, and medicolegal charting. Exceptional regulatory rigor.

assessment: The module check items and the 14-question final course quiz test the stated learning objectives with exact alignment. Every item has exactly one defensible correct answer, plausible distractors reflecting common clinical misconceptions, and thorough explanatory rationales. The weight distribution appropriately balances physiology (36%), evidence appraisal (29%), and regulatory safety (29%). No weak, ambiguous, or broken items were identified.
educationalQuality: Educational quality is exceptional. Learning objectives across all seven modules are measurable and action-oriented. The curriculum moves systematically from foundational organ-level endocrinology to clinical pattern recognition, pharmacology, trial appraisal, and regulatory compliance. Content is dense and completely free of padding or ungrounded promotional bias. Practical exercises, including sales-page audits and chart-note drafting, foster critical reasoning rather than passive recall.

learningTime.basis: Calculated independently across 7 modules: 7 opening videos (8.5 minutes total runtime) + 48 lesson text and audio script blocks (approx. 24,000 words at 140 wpm reading/listening = 171 minutes) + 35 interactive tool and scenario exercises (at 2.5 minutes each = 87.5 minutes) + 7 module formative quizzes and checks (10 minutes) + 14-item final certification exam (15 minutes).
learningTime.note: Total independent learning time of 290 minutes (~4.8 hours) matches the package's 289-minute planning estimate. The course explicitly disclaims awarding CME or CE credit at this time.

localization: Only one locale is requested (en). No translated edition is being claimed. Within the English edition, regional regulatory variations are systematically delineated across six jurisdictions (US, GB, EU, PT, BR, AE) using modular, authority-specific notes.

Maintain the current course boundaries excluding all dosing schedules, titration protocols, product concentrations, and peptide stacking formulas from learner-facing content.

Ensure all dynamic international register lookups (EDE, ANVISA, INFARMED) that could not be mechanically verified in automated claim-support checks are backed by static, timestamped PDF captures in the audit archive before final publishing.
